info.name: NeighborHub Authentication API
info.description:
Complete Postman collection for the NeighborHub Authentication API.

Covers all 7 endpoints with success, validation failure, authentication failure, and rate-limit scenarios.

## Setup

1. Import this collection and the `NeighborHub.local.postman_environment.json` environment.
2. Select the **NeighborHub Local** environment.
3. Start the Laravel development server: `php artisan serve`
4. Run the **00 - Setup** folder first to generate unique test data.
5. Run folders in order for sequential flows.

## Environment Variables

- `base_url`: API base (default: `http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/v1`)
- `access_token` / `second_access_token`: Populated by successful register/login
- `test_email` / `test_password`: Generated at runtime
- `reset_token`: Must be manually set from your local mail channel after running forgot-password
- `inactive_user_email` / `inactive_user_password`: Requires a locally prepared inactive-user fixture

## Password Policy

Minimum 15 characters, maximum 64 characters, confirmation required.

exec: // Collection-level pre-request: generate unique test data if not already set.

item.description: Initialize runtime test data. Run this folder first. The collection-level pre-request script generates unique emails, passwords, and device names into environment variables when they are empty.

item.name: Generate Test Data
item.description: Sends a no-op request to trigger the collection-level pre-request script which populates test environment variables. Verify variables are set after running.

exec: pm.test('Generated password meets minimum length (15+)', function () {

item.description:
Registration endpoint scenarios. POST /api/v1/auth/register

Fields: name (required), email (required, unique), phone (optional), password (required, 15-64 chars, confirmed), password_confirmation (required), device_name (required).

item.name: Register - Success - 201
item.description: Register a new user with valid data. Saves access_token and registered_user_id.

exec: pm.test('User resource has expected fields', function () {
pm.test('Password is not exposed in response', function () {
pm.test('Save access_token and user ID', function () {

item.name: Register - Missing Required Fields - 422
item.description: Omit all required fields. Expects validation errors.

item.name: Register - Duplicate Email - 422
item.description: Uses the same test_email already registered in the success request.

item.name: Register - Injected Role and is_active Ignored - 201
item.description: Attempts to inject role=super_admin and is_active=false. The server ignores these and returns role=resident, is_active=true.

exec: pm.test('Role is resident despite injection', function () {
pm.test('is_active is true despite injection', function () {

item.name: 02 - Login
item.description:
Login endpoint scenarios. POST /api/v1/auth/login

Fields: email (required), password (required), device_name (required).

Rate limited: 5/min per email+IP, 30/min per IP.

item.name: Login - Success - 200
item.description: Login with the registered test user. Saves access_token.

item.name: Login - Wrong Password - 401
item.description: Uses correct email but wrong password. Returns same generic 401 as missing user.

item.name: Login - Nonexistent Email - 401
item.description: Uses an email that does not exist. Returns the same generic 401 as wrong password to prevent account enumeration.

exec: pm.test('Same generic error message as wrong password', function () {

item.name: Login - Inactive Account - 401
item.description:
REQUIRES LOCAL FIXTURE: You must manually create an inactive user in your local database before running this request.

Set environment variables:
- inactive_user_email
- inactive_user_password

Example SQL:
INSERT INTO users (name, email, password, role, is_active, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('Inactive User', 'inactive@example.test', '<bcrypt_hash>', 'resident', 0, NOW(), NOW());

The response is the same generic 401 as wrong password — the server does not reveal that the account is inactive.

exec: pm.test.skip('Skipped: inactive_user_email and inactive_user_password not set');
pm.test('Same generic error (no account-existence leak)', function () {

item.name: 03 - Current User
item.description:
GET /api/v1/auth/me

Requires auth:sanctum + EnsureUserIsActive middleware.

Returns UserResource: id, name, email, phone, avatar, role, is_active, email_verified_at, created_at.

item.name: Me - Authenticated - 200
item.description: Requires a valid access_token from a prior register or login.

item.name: 04 - Logout
item.description:
POST /api/v1/auth/logout

Requires auth:sanctum. Revokes only the current token. Returns 204 No Content.

item.name: Logout - Success - 204
item.description: Logs out the current session. Saves the revoked token for follow-up verification, then clears access_token.

item.name: Me - Revoked Token - 401
item.description: Verify that the just-revoked token no longer grants access.

item.name: 05 - Change Password
item.description:
PUT /api/v1/auth/password

Requires auth:sanctum + EnsureUserIsActive.

Fields: current_password (required), password (required, 15-64 chars, confirmed, must differ from current), password_confirmation (required).

Returns 204 No Content. Revokes all other tokens.

item.name: Login - Get Fresh Token for Password Change
item.description: Re-login to get a fresh access_token before password change tests.

item.name: Me - Current Token Still Valid After Password Change - 200
Login - New Password Works - 200
item.description: After a successful password change, update test_password to new_password for subsequent requests.

item.name: 06 - Forgot Password
item.description:
POST /api/v1/auth/forgot-password

Fields: email (required).

Always returns the same generic 200 response regardless of whether the email exists. Rate limited: 3/hr per email, 10/hr per IP.

item.name: Forgot Password - Existing Email - 200
item.description: After running, retrieve the reset token from your local mail channel (log file, Mailtrap, etc.) and set the reset_token environment variable.

exec: pm.expect(pm.response.json().message).to.eql('If an account exists for this email, a password reset link has been sent.');
pm.test('No token or data in response', function () {

item.name: Forgot Password - Nonexistent Email - 200
item.description: Same generic response as existing email. Does not reveal account existence.

exec: pm.expect(pm.response.json().message).to.eql('If an account exists for this email, a password reset link has been sent.');

item.name: 07 - Reset Password
item.description:
POST /api/v1/auth/reset-password

Fields: email (required), token (required), password (required, 15-64 chars, confirmed), password_confirmation (required).

The reset_token must be obtained from the local mail channel after running Forgot Password. Rate limited: 5/15min per IP.

item.name: Reset Password - Success - 200
item.description:
PREREQUISITE: Run 'Forgot Password - Existing Email' first, then retrieve the reset token from your local mail channel (log driver, Mailtrap, etc.) and set the reset_token environment variable.

All existing access tokens are revoked on successful reset.

exec: pm.test.skip('Skipped: reset_token not set. Run Forgot Password first and set reset_token from your mail channel.');

item.name: Reset Password - Missing Email - 422
item.description: Omit the email field from reset password request. Expects 422 with email validation error.

item.name: 08 - Authentication Sequences
item.description: End-to-end ordered flows. Run requests within each sub-folder in sequence.

item.name: Registration Flow
item.description: Register → Me → Logout → Verify revoked → Login again.

item.name: Multi-Device Password Change Flow
item.description: Login device 1 → Login device 2 → Change password with device 1 → Verify device 1 still works → Verify device 2 revoked → Old password fails → New password works.

exec: // Register this user first via API
if (pm.response.code === 201) { pm.environment.set('access_token', pm.response.json().data.access_token); pm.test('Registered 201', function(){ pm.response.to.have.status(201); }); }

item.name: Password Reset Flow
item.description:
Forgot password → (manual token setup) → Reset → Verify tokens revoked → Old password fails → New password works.

After step 1, retrieve the reset token from your local mail channel and set the reset_token environment variable before running step 3.

item.name: 2. CHECKPOINT - Set reset_token
item.description:
STOP HERE. Retrieve the reset token from your configured local mail channel (log file, Mailtrap, etc.) and set the reset_token environment variable before continuing.

This is not a real API request — it serves as a checkpoint reminder.

exec: pm.test.skip('Set reset_token from mail channel before continuing');
pm.test('401 (token revoked by reset)', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(401); });

item.name: 09 - Rate Limits - Manual
item.description:
MANUAL RATE-LIMIT TESTS

These requests intentionally trigger 429 Too Many Attempts responses. Do NOT run them as part of the normal flow — they will consume your rate-limit quota.

Rate limiter thresholds (from implementation):
- auth-register: 5/hour per IP
- auth-login-email: 5/minute per email+IP
- auth-login-ip: 30/minute per IP
- auth-forgot-email: 3/hour per email
- auth-forgot-ip: 10/hour per IP
- auth-reset: 5/15min per IP

Use unique test identities. Wait for windows to expire before re-running.

item.name: Login Email Rate Limit (6 requests, 6th = 429)
item.description:
Sends 5 failed login attempts + 1 more to trigger the auth-login-email limiter (5/min per email+IP). The 6th request should return 429.

Run this MANUALLY. Uses rate_limit_email to avoid affecting your test user.

exec: pm.test('Request ' + count + ' should be 429 (rate limited)', function () {

item.name: Forgot Password Email Rate Limit (4 requests, 4th = 429)
item.description:
Sends 3 forgot-password requests + 1 more to trigger the auth-forgot-email limiter (3/hr per email). The 4th should return 429.

Run this MANUALLY. Uses rate_limit_email.

item.name: Register Rate Limit (6 requests, 6th = 429)
item.description:
auth-register: 5/hour per IP. Send 5 register requests with unique emails + 1 more. The 6th should return 429.

Run MANUALLY. Each request uses a unique email generated in pre-request.

item.name: Reset Password Rate Limit (6 requests, 6th = 429)
item.description:
auth-reset: 5/15min per IP. Send 5 reset requests + 1 more. Uses invalid token so each returns 422 until the 6th returns 429.

Run MANUALLY.

item.name: Login IP Rate Limit (31 requests, 31st = 429)
item.description: auth-login-ip: 30/minute per IP. Send 30 failed login attempts with unique email addresses (so the email-based 5/min limiter is not triggered) + 1 more request. The 31st request should return 429.\n\nRun this MANUALLY.

exec: pm.test('Request ' + count + ' should be 429 (IP rate limited)', function () {

item.name: Forgot Password IP Rate Limit (11 requests, 11th = 429)
item.description: auth-forgot-ip: 10/hour per IP. Send 10 forgot-password requests with unique email addresses (so the email-based 3/hour limiter is not triggered) + 1 more request. The 11th request should return 429.\n\nRun this MANUALLY.

exec: pm.test('Request ' + count + ' should be 429 (IP rate limited)', function () {

item.name: 12 - Reactions
item.description:
Post Reaction endpoint.

POST /api/v1/communities/{community_id}/posts/{post_id}/react

Toggle behavior:
- First request with a type creates the reaction (201).
- Changing the type updates the existing reaction (200).
- Repeating the same type removes the reaction (200).

Supported types: like, love, support, helpful, celebrate.

Requires active resident membership in the community.

item.name: React to Post
item.description:
Toggle a reaction on a post.

First request creates (201). Changing type updates (200). Same type again removes (200).

Requires active resident membership.
